text: ChatGPT, Claude and Grok all crashed at the same time.
And suddenly, humanity had to use its own brain.
Over thirty-five thousand people in America reported ChatGPT problems.
Not a war. Not a flood. Just a loading spinner.
Picture one of them, staring at a blank screen.
He has an email to write. He opens the chat. Nothing.
He tries again. Nothing. He tries a third time, like that changes anything.
Somewhere, a developer remembers that code used to be typed by hand.
Meanwhile, the internet did what it does best.
It joked. If you rent your brain, what happens when the landlord goes offline?
And we ran straight to them. Like nothing happened.
Humanity survived ice ages, plagues, and dial-up.
You see, we didn't lose a tool. We lost our excuse to think.
Subscribe to Goodchaos, before your brain regrets it.
